title: The CTAP2 crate must not be the one that needs the exception
description:
deny.toml denies ring, aws-lc-rs and aws-lc-sys, with exactly one
wrapper exception: ctap-hid-fido2. That exception exists because the
crate is already in the tree, not because it was chosen.

WHAT THE CRATE IS USED FOR TODAY: get_fidokey_devices() and HidParam.
HID device listing, and nothing else. prove() is unimplemented, so the
attestor enumerates candidates it can never prove and the ring edge buys
an enumeration.

WHY THIS BELONGS TO persona-qbnm.3 RATHER THAN TO DEPENDENCY HYGIENE:
the crate choice is not settled until something actually speaks CTAP2 to
a key, and that is qbnm.3's job. Whatever crate does it is the one this
project lives with, so "reaches ring through nothing" is a selection
criterion alongside the ones that are about function.

WORTH KNOWING BEFORE SHOPPING: talking to a hardware key does not
require us to do much cryptography. The key signs; the host sends CBOR
over HID. The host-side crypto is the PIN/pinUvAuth protocol -- ECDH on
P-256, HKDF, AES-CBC, HMAC-SHA-256 -- and every one of those is already
in this tree or is a RustCrypto crate away: p256, hkdf, aes, hmac, sha2.
So a raw-HID crate plus the protocol is a real option and not an
unbounded one, if no existing crate fits.

THE EXCEPTION IS NARROW BY CONSTRUCTION. cargo-deny's wrappers form
allows ring only as a direct dependency of ctap-hid-fido2; a second path
to ring fails the check, including a second path through the same crate.
So this does not silently widen while it waits.
acceptance_criteria: Either ctap-hid-fido2 is replaced by a crate that reaches ring through nothing, or the wrapper exception in deny.toml is recorded as permanent with the reason it cannot be removed.
